title: Container Bookings: Goodwill on Customer Roll Fees
content:
A customer of Container Bookings may ask the desk to take back, as goodwill, a customer roll fee charged on one of its bookings. This page describes that goodwill and the tool that records it.

## What the goodwill does

At the request of the verified customer, the desk may waive a customer roll fee entry of a booking as goodwill. A waiver cancels the fee entry in its entirety and never a part of it. It is written as a single waiver entry that carries the full amount of the fee entry and refers to that fee entry as the one it cancels. Whether the desk may grant it is decided under the goodwill conditions of Container Bookings that apply to customer roll fees; where they are not met, no waiver entry is written.

## Effect on the account

The waiver entry, coded `waiver`, appears in the charge history beside the fee it cancels, and the booking's outstanding charges fall by the waived amount. The cancelled fee entry remains in the history unaltered, and the booking's sailing, containers and status do not change.

## Recording the waiver

The tool is `waive_customer_roll_fee_66cbaf18`, run by the agent. It does not appear among the agent's tools until it is unlocked through `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, after which the agent calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

| Parameter | Meaning | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `booking_id` | the booking whose fee is being waived, by the reference number that the booking lookup gives for the verified customer | identifier |
| `customer_id` | the customer reference number of the booking party, as given by the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `reference_event_id` | the reference number of the customer roll fee entry being cancelled, as shown in the charge history or in the receipt of the charge that booked it | identifier |
| `waiver_usd` | the amount waived, in US dollars | positive decimal, two places; extra digits rounded half-to-even to two places |

Each call enters one waiver, dated on the day of the call; the entry takes the booking's equipment type and no container count, the amount supplied being the whole of it.

## Receipt

The answer is a text rendering of a dictionary: `booking_event_id` of the waiver entry, `booking_id`, `charge_code` (always `waiver`), `reference_event_id` of the fee entry cancelled, `amount_usd` waived (two decimals), `event_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `charges_due_usd` outstanding afterwards. A `booking_event_id` in the answer confirms that the waiver is on the account.
